subject.title: [RFC] Agent Teleconference — minimum-viable scoped meeting primitive with working prototype

question: Should OpenClaw accept a first-party scoped agent teleconference lifecycle now, and if so should it land as core CLI verbs or as a plugin/ClawHub package backed by any missing SDK seams?
rationale: The request changes public CLI shape, persisted meeting/transcript state, cross-agent authorization, and possibly config schema, so the next step depends on maintainer product and security intent rather than a safe autonomous fix.

options.title: Keep as scoped RFC first
options.body: Keep this issue open and require the next PR or design note to resolve storage, transcript privacy, authorization, and handoff layering before implementation.

options.title: Sponsor narrow core CLI
options.body: Approve a small core implementation with dial/pickup/send/wrap/list/show/transcript only, using current session/delivery primitives and focused lifecycle tests.

options.title: Route to plugin or ClawHub
options.body: Declare teleconference orchestration optional and ask for a plugin/ClawHub package, with a separate core issue only for any missing SDK seam.

recommendation.title: Keep as scoped RFC first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and require the next PR or design note to resolve storage, transcript privacy, authorization, and handoff layering before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: He left the existing scoping comment and is the clearest decision owner in the issue discussion and adjacent agent history.
